question_record.context: A security incident involving suspicious WMI process creation was reported on the machine `vnevado-win11u`. This machine also saw multiple suspicious processes including `curl http://vectorsandarrows.com`, `vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all`, and `get-userprttoken.ps1` on 2024-06-20. The incident is related to potential malware activity which might be using WMI to spawn new processes and further infect the machine.
question_record.question: During the investigation of this incident, there was a possible attempt to access a Primary Refresh Token (PRT). Can you identify the AadDeviceId of the host involved in this end alert?
solution: A suspicious WMI process creation was observed involving the user with SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522`.
There was a possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT) on the host with AadDeviceId `e5799261-6720-4297-961e-bd9ca4275033`.

117.name: Suspicious WMI process creation
117.description: Suspicious WMI process creation was observed on the machine. Malware frequently use WMI to spawn new processes, breaking process trees and further infecting a machine.

82.name: Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT)
82.description:
Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) has been detected. A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

For more information, read the Activity profile: Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/e4aad043-a273-4f88-b65e-fdfc3996ec92/analystreport?

steps.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'Command_File_Mention' AND o.Concept = 'Account_SID'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s,%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501
